sources.entry: changedetection.io - Stay up-to-date with web-site content changes. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Python/Docker
changedetection.io | Website change detection and price monitoring

summary.one_liner: changedetection.io is an open-source, self-hostable tool that monitors web pages for content, price, and restock changes and sends notifications when they occur.
summary.what_it_does: Watches URLs on a schedule and detects changes in page text, HTML, PDFs, and JSON API responses. Filters can target content with XPath, CSS selectors, JSONPath, jq, or regular expressions, and a Visual Selector helps pick elements (when Playwright is enabled). Users can switch between a fast non-JS HTTP fetcher and a Chrome-based fetcher, and run browser steps such as logging in or clicking buttons before checking. Notifications are sent through the apprise library to many services (e.g., Discord, email, Slack, Telegram, webhooks), with Jinja2 templating and optional screenshots. The README also describes optional AI features that use a user-supplied LLM (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers) to filter changes and write summaries, plus a REST API, Excel/plain-text import, and per-watch proxies.
use_cases: monitor product prices and restock alerts
get notified when a web page or government site updates
track changes to PDFs or legal documents
watch JSON API responses and turn changes into RSS or webhooks
monitor careers pages for new job postings
how_to_run: docker compose up -d (from a clone of the repository)
docker run -d --restart always -p "127.0.0.1:5000:5000" -v datastore-volume:/datastore --name changedetection.io dgtlmoon/changedetection.io
notable: Filters include XPath 1.0, CSS, JSONPath, jq, and lxml regex, plus JSON embedded in HTML pages
Optional AI change-detection rules and summaries via any LLM, including local Ollama or OpenAI-compatible servers
Notification support across many services through the apprise library
Full REST API with OpenAPI spec and a Chrome extension for adding pages
Runs on Raspberry Pi and ARM devices per the README
caveats: Browser-based (JS) fetching and the Visual Selector require Playwright or WebDriver to be enabled
AI features send page content to third-party providers if enabled, and API costs are the user's responsibility
The README also promotes a paid hosted subscription ($8.99/month) that includes proxies and Chrome; this is separate from the open-source software
keywords: get notified when a site changes
